title: Evaluation of an e-learning program "Basic Course in Suicide Prevention in the Healthcare System"
summary: The planned study will evaluate a newly developed e-learning program on suicide prevention in the healthcare sector. The program is designed for healthcare professionals who may come into contact with people at risk of suicide as part of their professional duties. The goal of the program is to provide basic knowledge and skills regarding suicide prevention in the healthcare sector and to encourage participants to apply this knowledge confidently and responsibly in their daily professional practice. In the study, participants will be randomly assigned to one of three experimental groups. One group will complete the e-learning program. A second group watches an alternative online lecture, while the third group initially receives no training. Both control groups will also receive access to the e-learning program once the study is complete. Following their respective study conditions, participants complete online questionnaires. These assess their subjective knowledge about suicide prevention, their confidence in their own abilities when dealing with people at risk of suicide, their attitudes toward suicide prevention, and their ability to recognize appropriate responses to statements made by people at risk of suicide. In addition, information regarding the participants’ personal and professional backgrounds will be obtained. Participants in the e-learning condition will also be asked to evaluate the e-learning program. By comparing the three experimental groups, the study aims to determine how effective the e-learning program is compared to an alternative learning option or to no training at all.
conditions: Suicide prevention in the healthcare sector
